subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits tool-call-shaped assistant text instead of structured toolCall/toolUse content?
rationale: Current source intentionally combines warning-only diagnostics, limited compatibility promotion, and scoped Gateway HTTP enforcement; choosing stricter rejection, forced retry, or default promotion changes both the security boundary and local-model compatibility contract.

options.title: Define bounded enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and then implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Document this as provider/model incompatibility and accept that fake tool-call text can still reach transcripts or visible replies without a real tool call.

options.title: Split broader claim checks
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and keep natural-language success claims under the broader response-gate or claim-ledger tracking items.

recommendation.title: Define bounded enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and then implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a default agent-runtime security and compatibility policy choice, and steipete is the best available routing candidate from current source history and prior issue review context.
